- When sentiment is consistently bullish (1.00) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2% relative to model output.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to forecasted values following such events.
- If sentiment is bearish (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in the final 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon; apply a slight upward bias (0.5–1.5%) to the last 5–7 forecasted values.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; if sentiment drops after day 10–15, reduce forecast slope downward by 0.2–0.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
